newsitem.title: LATVIA: Lithuanian PM sees five pct 1997 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian PM sees five pct 1997 GDP growth.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius forecast that gross domestic product (GDP) in the Baltic state would grow by five percent in 1997, he told Latvian newspaper Diena in an interview published on Wednesday.
He also said Lithaunia would try boost export industries.
Vagnorius, of the right-wing Homeland Union, was elected in November.
"Lithuania's overall indicators have not worsened. I forecast that GDP in 1997 will rise by five percent," Vagnorius told Diena.
Final figures for 1996 GDP have not yet been published but GDP growth over the first half of last year was 3.1 percent.
Vagnorius said one of the government's key aims was to boost the export sector, and 10.5 million litas has been set aside as export credit guarantees.
"After around seven years, 70 percent of the national economy will come from exports," he added.
He noted that the textile, machine manufacturing and timber industries could be the best placed to benefit in the future.
Vagnorius has also pledged to speed up privatisation and economic reforms in Lithuania, which many observers say has lagged its Baltic neighbours, Latvia and Estonia.
"I of course acknowledge that in Estonia purchasing power is higher than in Lithuania which automatically gurantees higher standards and consumption," Vagnorius said.
"On other indicators, all the Baltic states are developing similarly which of course is dependent on their similar starting positions," he said.
